scope: Proposition 15.1 (Static cap comparison) of the manuscript “Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Critical-mixing-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 117. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a field radius R < ∞, an error tolerance η > 0, and a geometric ratio in (0, 1). There is a sufficiently small upper scale p0 > 0 such that, with probability tending to one, simultaneously over a geometric list of caps p ≤ p0 with np3 ≥ c √ log n and all h ∈ PpRn satisfying ∥h∥ ≤ Rp2Mp, one has | log Zp(h) − log Zsp p (h)| ≤ ηkp, ∥Ppmp(h) − ap(h)∥ ≤ ηMp, mp(h) = ∇ log Zp(h). (15.9) The projected norm tails proved above hold, with a decreased positive exponential constant, under these cube posteriors and under the uncapped zero-field cube posterior. The statement remains valid for any fixed finite collection of auxiliary geometric cap lists. The zero-field concentration and density estimates used in the proof also allow bounded scalar modifications of the cap interaction whose spherical saddle gaps remain comparable to p2.
